name: Run the reports against stock and asset records — what is held, what moved, what is owed back, and what was disposed of
priorityReason: The reorder list is what buying is triggered from, and the count variance is what a store is checked by.

goal.actor: the School Admin, Accounts or the Principal
goal.capability: to run the stock or asset report I need for the period, item, location or branch I choose
goal.outcome: I know what is held, what moved, what is still owed back and what has gone

secondaryActors.involvement: Reads the stock valuation, the reorder list, the asset register and the depreciation schedule.
Reads the count variance, the outstanding advances, and the disposals with their approvals and proceeds.

preconditions.condition: Stock items and assets exist to report against.
An authenticated session exists and the acting user holds the permission for the report.
The branch is known, since every report is scoped to it.

postConditions: The report was selected from the same catalogue every other report is selected from.
The period, the item, the category, the location or the branch were set before it ran.
It ran against the stock and asset records, so the figures are the ones those records hold.
The reorder list showed items at or below their reorder level, which is what buying is triggered from.
The count variance showed the reasons and the approvers, since a variance with neither is a discrepancy nobody investigated.
The disposals report showed the approvals and the proceeds, because each disposal names an approver.
A stock valuation was shown only where stock is held at value, and a depreciation schedule only where a book value exists.
It was read on screen, and taken away in print or as a file by the one output route.

businessRules.rule: Every report in this feature is selected from the same catalogue as every other report. The reporting for the inventory and asset module lives here.
The reader sets the period, the item, the category, the location or the branch before the report runs.
The reports run against the stock and asset records.
A stock valuation is shown only where stock is held at value. No feature in the document holds a price for a stock item, so the valuation column reads as unavailable rather than as zero.
The count variance report shows the reason and the approver for each variance. A variance with neither is a discrepancy nobody investigated.
The depreciation schedule requires a book value, and nothing in the document calculates depreciation. The schedule reads as unavailable rather than showing a figure nothing produces.
The disposals report shows the approvals and the proceeds, since every disposal names an approver and a disposal nobody approved is what the report exists to reveal.
A report reads and writes nothing. A wrong balance is corrected by a stock adjustment, never from a report.
A report is taken away in print or as a file by the one output route.

sideEffects.effect: Every report is taken away by the one output route.
The stock reports read the items, receipts, issues and adjustments.
The reorder list is what a stock request is raised from.
The count variance reads the adjustments and their approvals.
The asset reports read the register and its assignments.
The disposals report reads the disposals and their approvals.
Running a report is written to the audit trail.

departures.requirement: A stock valuation and a depreciation figure read as unavailable where nothing produces them. Neither is shown as zero, which would be a figure the reader would act on.
No variance is reported without the reason and the approver recorded against it.
No report changes a balance or an asset record.

openQuestions.question: No feature holds a price for a stock item, so the stock valuation report cannot produce a figure.
openQuestions.assumption: Unresolved. Accounts are named as reading it.

openQuestions.question: Nothing calculates depreciation, so the depreciation schedule cannot produce a figure, and neither can the gain or loss on a disposal.
openQuestions.assumption: Unresolved, and it blocks the disposal use case as well.

openQuestions.question: No feature creates rooms, and the assets-by-location report groups by them.
Is the asset register readable by the Principal, given only Accounts are listed?
openQuestions.assumption: Not as modelled, per the document's reader list.

conventionsApplied.name: session-and-authentication
conventionsApplied.rule: Every use case except the login use case assumes an authenticated session. Sign out is available on every screen. An expired or invalid session returns the user to the login screen with the message "Your session has ended. Please sign in again."

conventionsApplied.name: role-based-access
conventionsApplied.rule: Access is enforced server-side on every request, not only by hiding menu items. A request for a record outside the actor's permitted scope returns a 403 and the message "You do not have permission to view this record." A use case states additions and restrictions only.

conventionsApplied.name: branch-scope
conventionsApplied.rule: Every record carries a branch ID. Users see only their own branch unless the use case states otherwise. Super Admin, School Admin and Principal may switch branch from the header.

conventionsApplied.name: list-screens
conventionsApplied.rule: Every list supports search, column sort and page-size selection. Default page size 25; default sort is most recent first. Filters are applied before printing or exporting.

conventionsApplied.name: print-and-pdf
conventionsApplied.rule: Every report and list offers Print and Download as PDF, honouring the filters currently applied. Each output carries the school name, branch, academic session, report title, filter summary, generation timestamp and the name of the user who generated it.

conventionsApplied.name: audit-trail
conventionsApplied.rule: Every create, update, deactivation, approval and reversal writes to the audit log: actor, role, timestamp, record type, record ID, before and after values, and IP address. Audit entries are never editable.

conventionsApplied.name: validation-and-messages
conventionsApplied.rule: Field-level errors appear inline beneath the field on blur and on submit. Errors that block the whole action appear as a banner at the top of the form. Successful actions show a toast. No action succeeds silently.

conventionsApplied.name: money
conventionsApplied.rule: All monetary values are stored as fixed-point decimals in the smallest currency unit, never as floating point. Displayed as PKR with a thousands separator and two decimal places. Rounding is half-up at the line.

conventionsApplied.name: dates-times-numbers
conventionsApplied.rule: Dates display as DD-MM-YYYY; date and time as DD-MM-YYYY HH:mm in 24-hour form. Times are school-local. Phone numbers are stored in the registered mobile format.

conventionsApplied.name: language
conventionsApplied.rule: All user-visible strings come from a resource file. No hard-coded text in any screen.

conventionsApplied.name: screen-states
conventionsApplied.rule: Every list, dashboard tile and report defines four states: loading, empty, error and populated. The empty state names what is missing and links to the action that creates it.

conventionsApplied.name: default-performance-and-retention
conventionsApplied.rule: Unless a use case states otherwise: a screen loads within 2 seconds and a save completes within 2 seconds at 200 concurrent users; lists paginate above 100 rows; financial and student records are retained 7 years; audit and message logs 12 months; every screen is usable at a 360 px viewport. Fill the non-functional field only to depart from this.

conventionsApplied.name: default-trigger
conventionsApplied.rule: Unless a use case states otherwise, the trigger is: the user navigates to the screen and initiates the action. Fill the Triggers field only where a scheduled job, an event in another module, or an inbound external call also starts it.
